workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§191–193
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§191–193: The Guard Ordained and the Fires at Sa'ari-Keger
part: §§191–193 — The Guard Ordained and the Fires at Sa'ari-Keger
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§191–193, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Three sections of army and war. §191 organises the host into thousands, hundreds and tens, names six cherbi, and enrols the guard: eighty night guards and seventy day guards, with sons and brothers chosen for skill and looks, Arqai-Qasar's brave men and Ögöle-Cherbi over the day guards. §192 gives the guard its duties (who lies around the tents, who stands at the door, who goes to his post, who sits, and the rota of three nights) and ends as the host rides out against the Naiman. §193 gives the date (the sixteenth day of the first month of summer in the Year of the Rat), the march up the Kerülen with Jebe and Qubilai in the van, a skirmish at Sa'ari-Keger in which a horse is lost, the Naiman scouts' remark that the Mongol geldings are lean, Dodai-Cherbi's plan of the five fires for each man, and the report the scouts carry away. The grammar to watch is the optative in -tuγai ("let them …") that carries §192, the converb chains in -žu/-žü, the reflexive -jan/-jen, and the reciprocal -ldu-. Several lines are hard, above all the soup passage in §192 and the clause with γol-dur in §193, and the notes say so. The Mongol readings follow Shiratori; the English is a first drafting.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

morph.gloss: to approve, say 'right' (stem read from the Ming) [道是着]

sentences.i: Approving this word of Belgütei Noyan,
sentences.n: nojan-u is the genitive of nojan, a title (Ming 官人, 'official'): 'of Belgütei the lord', which I give as Belgütei Noyan as in the last part. üge-ji is üge 'word' with the accusative -ji (the Ming 行 marks the object). žöbšiježü is a converb in -žü, 'approving' (Ming 道是着, 'saying it is right'); the stem žöbšiye- is read from the Ming. The subject, Chinggis, comes in the next unit, so this converb hangs forward. What Belgütei's word was is not given in this part.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan aba baγ̇uγ̇ad Abžiγa-Köteger-eče ködölžü Qalqa-jin Ornuγ̇u-jin Keltegei-Qada baγ̇užu

words.reading: 阿卜只中合-闊帖格舌列徹 Abžiγa-Köteger-eče

glyphs.s: 阿卜只中合-闊帖格舌列徹

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, circle-hunt having camped, from Abžiγa-Köteger moving, Qalqa river's Ornuγ̇u's Keltegei-Qada camping,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan held a circle hunt, moved on from Abjiya-Köteger, and camped at Keltegei-Qada in Ornu'u on the Qalqa river,
sentences.n: Three converbs run on from here: baγuγad ('having …', -γad), ködölžü ('moving', -žü) and baγužu ('camping'); the finite verb is far off, at tüšibe. baγu- is Ming 下, 'go down, alight, camp'; with aba, 'circle hunt' (Ming 圍獵), I take it as 'pitched camp for the hunt', which is uncertain. Abžiγa-Köteger-eče has the ablative -eče, 'from'. Qalqa-jin Ornuγu-jin Keltegei-Qada is a genitive chain read from the right (-jin is the genitive after a vowel): the Ming calls Qalqa a river and the other two places. Qada is not glossed apart from the name, so I do not translate it.

sentences.i: They counted up their numbers together and formed thousands there,
sentences.n: toγa-ban is toγa 'number' with the reflexive -ban 'one's own' (Ming 自的行). toγolaldužu is 'counting together' (the infix -ldu- is joint action, Ming 共). minγalažu is a verb made from the number miṅγan 'thousand': 'thousand-making' (Ming 千做着); the print writes the ṅ on one form and not the other, the sound is the same. The subject is not stated; I take it to be Chinggis and his officers.

sentences.t: miṅγan-u nojan žaγ̇un-u nojan harban-u nojan tende tüšibe.
sentences.l: Of-thousand lord, of-hundred lord, of-ten lord there appointed.
sentences.i: There he appointed lords of thousands, lords of hundreds and lords of tens.
sentences.n: Three genitives in a row (miṅγan-u, žaγun-u, harban-u), each before nojan 'lord': 'the thousand's lord'. The Ming reads each as 'officer of the thousand' (千的官人). tüšibe is the plain past of tüši- 'entrust, appoint' (Ming 委付), and the full stop closes the sentence that the converbs before it were building. The same verb ends units 5 and 7.

sentences.i: There too he appointed the cherbi.
sentences.n: čerbi is an office (Ming 官名, 'office name'); I do not know its duties and keep cherbi. čerbin-i has a linking n at the end of the stem and the accusative -i (Ming 行). kü is the particle 'also' (Ming 也).

sentences.t: Dodai-Čerbi, Doqolqu-Čerbi, Ögele-Čerbi, Tolun-Čerbi, Bučaran-Čerbi, Süiketü-Čerbi

sentences.l: Dodai-Čerbi, Doqolqu-Čerbi, Ögele-Čerbi, Tolun-Čerbi, Bučaran-Čerbi, Süiketü-Čerbi
sentences.i: Dodai-Cherbi, Doqolqu-Cherbi, Ögele-Cherbi, Tolun-Cherbi, Bucharan-Cherbi and Süiketü-Cherbi,
sentences.n: A list of six, kept whole. Each has -Čerbi as part of the name (Ming 人名 官名, 'personal name, office name'), so each man's name and his office are one word. Shiratori puts commas between the names and none after the last; the list is picked up by ede in the next unit. The spellings are as printed; I cannot check them against another edition.

sentences.i: These six cherbi he appointed there.
sentences.n: ede 'these' is the plural of ene (Ming 這(的每), 'these'), žirγoγan 'six'. čerbin-i has the accusative again. The unit sums the list above: six names, six cherbi.

sentences.t: Miṅγan miṅγalan, žaγ̇u žaγ̇ulan, harban harbalan baražu
sentences.l: Thousand thousand-made, hundred hundred-made, ten ten-made, finishing,
sentences.i: When the thousands, the hundreds and the tens had been made,
sentences.n: miṅγalan, žaγulan and harbalan are verbs made from the numbers (miṅγala- 'make a thousand', Ming 千做了) with a final -n, which I take as a converb 'having made' (uncertain: the Ming gives only 了, 'done'). baražu (Ming 了了着) is 'finishing, having completed'. The structure of the army is done; the guard follows.

sentences.t: najan kebteġül, dalan turγaγ̇ud tende kešigten ilγažu oroγ̇ulurun

morph.gloss: night guard (from kebte-, to lie down) [宿衞]

sentences.l: Eighty night-guards, seventy day-guards, there bodyguards choosing-out, when admitting,
sentences.i: When he enrolled the eighty night guards and seventy day guards, picking the bodyguards out there,
sentences.n: kebteġül is the night guard (Ming 宿衞), from kebte- 'lie down'; turγaγ (Ming 散班, 'scattered shift') I render 'day guard', an inference from §192, where these men give way to the night guard at sunset; the Ming does not say 'day'; kešigten (Ming 護衞, 'bodyguards') is the plural of a word in -tü, 'having', from kešig 'turn of duty'. najan is 'eighty', dalan 'seventy'. oroγulurun is oro- 'enter' + -γul- (causative) + -urun 'when': 'when making enter'. This is a dependent clause with no verb of its own: the sentence is finished only at oroγulba in unit 12, and the unit after this one starts a second 'when admitting' with its own objects. The numbers are given without a noun of count; I read them as the strength of each guard.

sentences.i: the sons and younger brothers of the lords of thousands, of hundreds and of the noyans,
sentences.n: Plurals in -d with the genitive -un: miṅγad-un 'of the thousand-lords' (Ming 千戶每的, 'thousand-household heads'), žaγud-un 'of the hundred-lords', nojad-un 'of the lords'. köġüd-i is 'sons' with the accusative; deġü-ner-i is 'younger brothers' (deġü with -ner, a plural used of kin) with the accusative. These are the objects of the oroγulurun that closes the next unit; the verb comes last.

sentences.t: utu duru-jin küġün-ü köġüd-i, deġü-ner-i oroγ̇ulurun

morph.gloss: 'just so' (uncertain; the stem is not known to me) [只那般]

sentences.l: Just-so, bare's person's sons-ACC, younger-brothers-ACC when admitting,
sentences.i: and likewise the sons and younger brothers of men without rank, when admitting them,
sentences.n: utu (Ming 只那般, 'just so') is not a word I can place; I read it as 'likewise', which is uncertain. duru-jin küġün-ü is 'of a plain person' (the Ming has 白身 for duru, 'bare body': a man with no rank), where -jin and -ü are genitives. Shiratori's comma after köġüd-i separates the two objects. oroγulurun closes this unit, and the objects in unit 10 hang on it too, so it governs two lines of kin.

sentences.t: erdemten beje šil saitan ilγažu oroγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: plural of -tu, having (uncertain; compare -ten in erdemten)

sentences.l: Skilled-ones, body, looks good-ones choosing-out, admitted.
sentences.i: he picked out the skilled and the fine-bodied and good-looking, and admitted them.
sentences.n: erdemten is erdem 'skill' (Ming 技能) + -ten, the plural of -tü 'having': 'those with skill'. beje (Ming 身材) is 'body, build' and šil (Ming 模樣) 'looks, appearance'; saitan is 'good ones' (plural), so I read beje šil saitan as 'good in build and looks'. This is the finite verb the chain was waiting for: oroγulba, with the full stop (the Ming has 敎入了). The sense of the whole passage: from the guard and from the sons and brothers of rank and of no rank, the able and handsome are chosen. The Ming gives 勒着 for the first ilγažu here, against 揀着 at the other occurrences; I take 勒 as a slip for 揀 (uncertain).

sentences.t: Tende Arγai-Qasar-i sojurγažu baγ̇atud-i ilγažu miṅγalatuγai;

words.reading: 阿舌兒中孩-中合撒舌里 Arγai-Qasar-i

glyphs.s: 阿舌兒中孩-中合撒舌里

sentences.l: There, Arγai-Qasar-ACC favouring, brave-ones-ACC choosing-out, let him make a thousand;
sentences.i: "Then, showing favour to Arqai-Qasar, let him pick out the brave men and make a thousand;
sentences.n: The print has a mark closing a speech at boltuγai in unit 15 but none opening it; I supply the opening here, at Tende, which is a guess. sojurγažu (Ming 恩賜着, 'granting favour') and Arγai-Qasar-i (Ming 行, accusative): the favour falls on Arqai-Qasar. baγatud-i is baγatur 'brave man' with plural -d and the accusative. miṅγalatuγai: -tuγai is the optative, 'let him …' (Ming 者). Who is to make the thousand is uncertain; I take it to be Arqai-Qasar, though his name carries the accusative, which would more naturally mark the one favoured. The semicolon is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: qadqulduγ̇an üdür emüne min-u baižu qadquldutuγai.

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀安 qadqulduγ̇an

morph.gloss: to fight (stem read from the Ming) [厮殺︀的]
I (the genitive stem is min-) [我的]
genitive: of, set after its noun

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀禿中孩 qadquldutuγai

glyphs.s: 中合惕中忽勒都︀禿中孩

sentences.l: Fighting-together day, front my standing, let-them-fight-together.
sentences.i: On the day of battle, let them stand before me and fight;
sentences.n: qadqulduγan is qadqul- (Ming 厮殺, 'fight', stem read from the Ming) + -ldu- (each other) + -γan, a participle (Ming 的, 'of') that makes it modify üdür 'day': 'the day of fighting'. emüne is 'front, before'; min-u is the genitive of bi 'I', so emüne min-u is 'my front'. baižu is 'standing' (Ming 立着). qadquldutuγai: optative -tuγai again, 'let them fight'.

sentences.t: Olon üdür turγaγ kešigten min-u boltuγai"

morph.gloss: I (the genitive stem is min-) [我的]
genitive: of, set after its noun

sentences.l: Many day, day-guards, bodyguards mine let-be"
sentences.i: and on the many other days let the day guards and bodyguards be mine."
sentences.n: olon üdür is 'many days' (Ming 多日), set against the one day of battle in the last unit: ordinary days. turγaγ kešigten min-u boltuγai is 'let the day guards and bodyguards be mine', min-u as a predicate genitive. The mark after boltuγai closes this decree (no opening mark in the print, see unit 13). The Ming glosses turγaγ here as 散班 and kešigten as 護衞, as before.

sentences.i: So he spoke, and it became a decree.
sentences.n: keġen 'saying' is a converb; žarliγ bolba (Ming 聖旨做了) is 'made an edict', the formula for putting a ruling into force. The formula žarliγ bolurun, 'when making a decree', which in house usage is 'issued a decree:', opens a speech; here the speech has come first and the closing formula follows.

morph.gloss: a man's name [人名 官名]

sentences.i: "Let the seventy day guards have Ögöle-Cherbi as their head;
sentences.n: A new speech opens, as the quotation mark before Dalan shows. aqalažu is aqa 'elder, senior' + -la- (make into) + -žu: 'making [him] the head' (Ming 爲頭着, 'taking as chief'). atuγai is a- 'be' + -tuγai, 'let them be' (Ming 有者). turγaγud-i, with the accusative, is the object of 'making head', so Ögöle-Cherbi is made head of the day guards. The print spells this man Ögöle here and Ögele in unit 6 (Han 斡歌列 against 斡格列); I take them to be one man and keep each spelling as printed, so the English differs too (uncertain).

words.reading: 中忽都︀思-中合勒潺-魯阿 Qudus-Qalčan-luγ̇a

glyphs.s: 中忽都︀思-中合勒潺-魯阿

morph.gloss: a man's name [人名 一同]

sentences.i: Take counsel together with Qudus-Qalchan, and remain," he said.
sentences.n: Ögöle-Cherbi is the one addressed, though adqun is a plural imperative (a courtesy plural, or the order also reaches Qudus-Qalčan; uncertain). Qudus-Qalčan-luγa has -luγa 'with' (Ming 一同, 'together'). ejetüldüžü (Ming 共商量着, 'consulting together'): the stem is not known to me; -ldü- is joint action. adqun is the imperative for several persons of a- 'be, stay' (Ming 住着), with -d- and -qun as in abčiradqun in the last part. The mark after adqun closes the speech; keġebe 'said' is the past of keġe-.

sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: basa is 'again' (Ming 再). žarliγ bolurun is bol- + -urun 'when', 'when making a decree'; the colon opens the speech, as in the last part, and the speech has a quotation mark in the next unit. I render it 'issued a decree:'.

morph.gloss: quiver (inferred from the Ming; printed Oorčin) [帶弓箭的]

sentences.i: "Quiver-bearers, day guards, bodyguards, cooks, door-keepers, grooms:
sentences.n: The print has Oorčin after the mark, a slip: the Han 中豁舌兒臣 and the Ming 帶弓箭的 ('bearer of bow and arrows') point to qorčin, and I read Qorčin. -či is the agent ending: baγurči 'cook' (Ming 厨子), egüdeči 'door-keeper' (Ming 把門的, from egüden 'door'), aγtači 'groom' (Ming 管馬的, from aγta 'gelding', house rendering). The quiver (qor) is my inference from the Ming. Six groups are addressed; the verbs come in the units after.

sentences.t: üdür kešig orožu naran šiṅgekü-jin urida kebteġül-e žailažu

morph.gloss: to give way, move aside [挪着]

sentences.l: Day shift entering, sun setting's before, to-night-guard giving-way,
sentences.i: when they come on the day shift, before sunset let them give way to the night guard,
sentences.n: kešig is the turn of duty (Ming 直班) and orožu 'entering' (Ming 入着). šiṅgekü-jin: šiṅge- 'sink' (the Ming has 落, 'fall', of the sun), the participle -kü, and the genitive -jin: 'of the sun's setting'. urida 'before' (Ming 先). kebteġül-e has the dative -e, 'to the night guard' (Ming 行). žailažu (Ming 挪着) is 'moving aside, giving way'. The optative they lead to is at qonotuγai in the next unit.

sentences.i: and go out to their own geldings and spend the night.
sentences.n: aγtas is the plural of aγta 'gelding' (Ming 騸馬); -tur(i) is the dative-locative with Shiratori's bracketed (i), and -jan means 'one's own' (Ming 自的行). 'At their own geldings' I read as 'where their horses are'; the Ming gives nothing more, so the place is a guess. γarun 'going out' (Ming 出); qonotuγai is qono- 'pass the night' + the optative -tuγai.

sentences.t: Kebteġül süni ger horčin kebtekün(i)-jen kebteġülžü

morph.gloss: night guard (from kebte-, to lie down) [宿衞]
to lie down [臥的每 自的行]

sentences.l: Night-guards, night, tent around lying-ones-own causing-to-lie,
sentences.i: Let the night guards at night set those of their own who lie down to lie around the tents,
sentences.n: kebteġül (night guard) and kebteġülžü ('causing to lie', with the causative -ġül-) come from the same stem kebte- 'lie down' (Ming 臥); the Ming (宿衞 / 敎臥着) plays on it too. ger is the tent (Ming 房子), horčin 'around' (Ming 周圍). kebtekün(i)-jen is kebte- + -kün (one who …) + -jen 'their own' (Ming 臥的每 自的行): 'their own lying ones', the part of the watch that sleeps. This and the next unit make one sentence: some lie around the tents, others stand at the door. The bracketed (i) in kebtekün(i)-jen may be the accusative -i, since the Ming 行 marks the object of kebteġülžü; the morphs leave it with the reflexive ending (uncertain).

morph.gloss: to stand [立的每 自的行]

sentences.i: and set their standing ones to stand at the door in turn.
sentences.n: egüden-dür is egüden 'door' + -dür 'at, in' (Ming 門裏). baiqun(i)-jan is bai- 'stand' + -qun (as in kebtekün) + -jan 'their own'. kešiglen is kešig 'turn' + -le- + -n, 'taking turns' (Ming 輪直着). baiγultuγai is bai- + -γul- (causative) + -tuγai: 'let them make stand': the causative is active, the night guards setting their own standing ones, as kebteġülžü in the unit before set the lying ones; the accusative (i) of baiqun(i)- is the object. The full stop closes the arrangement of the watch at night.

sentences.t: Qorčin turγaγ̇ud manaγar-i in-ü bidan-i sülen ideġesü

morph.gloss: quiver (inferred from the Ming) [帶弓箭的]
(case ending on a time word; sense not clear)
his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Quiver-bearers, day-guards, tomorrow his us soup if-eat,
sentences.i: As for the quiver-bearers and day guards: if tomorrow they give us soup to eat,
sentences.n: This is hard and uncertain. Word by word the Ming gives 明早 (tomorrow), 他的 (his, their), 咱 (us, inclusive, accusative), 湯 (soup), 喫呵 (if eat). ideġesü is the conditional of ide- 'eat', but 'us' is in the accusative, so 'if they feed us' and 'if we eat their soup' are both possible; I take the first. Who 'we' are is not stated. The -i of manaγar-i is a case ending on a word of time whose force I cannot press. Read the next unit with it. The Ming glosses turγaγud here 宿衞的(每), 'night guards', where it has 散班 elsewhere in this part; I keep 'day guards' and take the Ming here as a slip (uncertain).

morph.gloss: night guard (from kebte-, to lie down) [宿衞]
dative-locative: at, in (the Ming glosses it 'time') [時]

sentences.i: telling the night guard,
sentences.n: The hyphen after kebteġül- is the end of a line in the print (the Ming text turns the line there), and dür continues it. The Ming glosses dür as 時 'time', not 'to'; I read 'to the night guard' but 'at the night guard's hour' is possible. keleležü is 'speaking, telling' (Ming 說着), the stem kelele- being read from the Ming. This unit and the one before are uncertain; the sense seems to be that the day shift speaks to the night guard before the change.

sentences.t: qorčin turγaγ̇ud, baγ̇určin, egüdečin, mün mün mör-tür(i)-jen jabutuγai.

morph.gloss: quiver (inferred from the Ming) [帶弓箭的]

sentences.l: Quiver-bearers, day-guards, cooks, door-keepers, just just post-their-own-to let-them-go.
sentences.i: the quiver-bearers, day guards, cooks and door-keepers are each to go to their own posts.
sentences.n: baγurčin and egüdečin are plurals in -n of baγurči and egüdeči (Ming 每). mün mün (Ming 只 只) is 'just, just': I read 'each to his own'. mör-tür(i)-jen: mör is 'duty, post' (Ming 軄分, 'office share'), with the dative -tür(i) and the reflexive -jen. jabutuγai is jabu- 'go' + the optative.

words.reading: 撒兀舌鄰-都︀舌里-顏 Saγ̇urin-dur(i)-jan

sentences.i: Let them sit in their own places.
sentences.n: saγurin is 'seat, sitting place' (Ming 坐位) with -dur(i)-jan 'at their own'; saγutuγai is saγu- 'sit' + the optative. The pattern is the same as in the last unit, with a seat instead of a post.

sentences.t: Γurban süni γurban üdür kešig üdür(i)-jen daγ̇usčü

morph.gloss: to come to an end [盡了着]

sentences.l: Three nights, three days shift, days-their-own finishing,
sentences.i: When the three nights and three days of the shift are done,
sentences.n: γurban is 'three'. The Ming reads kešig as 輪直 'duty by turns' and üdür(i)-jen as 日自的行 'their own days'. daγusčü is daγus- 'come to an end' (Ming 盡了着) with -čü, a converb after a stem in -s. Whose shift lasts three days and nights is not said here; the next unit speaks of night guards, so I take it as theirs, but this is uncertain.

sentences.t: mün kü josu-γ̇ar γurban süni qonoldužu jeġüdgeldüžü süni kebteġül atuγai.

morph.gloss: to replace, relieve (stem inferred from the Ming) [替換着]
night guard (from kebte-, to lie down) [宿衞]

sentences.l: Just also by-custom three nights spending-night-together, replacing-each-other, night night-guard let-be.
sentences.i: let them, by the same rule, pass three nights together, relieve one another, and be the night guard at night.
sentences.n: josu-γar is josu 'custom, rule' (Ming 道理) + -γar 'by' (Ming 依着, instrumental). mün kü is 'just also' (Ming 只 也). qonoldužu 'passing the night together' has -ldu- (together); jeġüdgeldüžü (Ming 替換着, 'replacing, taking turns') has -ldü- (each other), and its stem I take from the Ming. süni kebteġül atuγai is 'at night, night guard, let them be'. How the rule of three nights fits with the day arrangement above I cannot tell.

sentences.t: Horčin kebtežü qonotuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Around lying, let-them-spend-the-night" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: Let them lie around and spend the night," he said, and made it a decree.
sentences.n: horčin kebtežü is 'lying around' (kebte- + -žü); qonotuγai 'let them spend the night'. The mark after qonotuγai closes the long decree opened before Qorčin. keġen žarliγ bolba is the closing formula, as in §191.

sentences.t: Tedüi miṅγan miṅγalan baražu čerbi tüšižü

morph.gloss: so much, that much; thereupon [那些]

sentences.l: That-much thousand thousand-making finishing, cherbi appointing,
sentences.i: Having thus made up the thousands, he appointed the cherbi,
sentences.n: tedüi is 'so much, that much' (Ming 那些) and the line repeats what §191 said, now with converbs (baražu, tüšižü) so that the sentence runs on into the guard again. The -žü of tüšižü is the same ending as -žu with the front vowel.

sentences.t: najan kebteġül dalan turγaγ̇ud kešigten oroγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: night guard (from kebte-, to lie down) [宿衞]

sentences.l: Eighty night-guards, seventy day-guards, shift-ones causing-to-enter,
sentences.i: and had the eighty night guards and seventy day guards, the ones on shift, enter,
sentences.n: kešigten is glossed 輪班 here, 'those who take turns', where in §191 it was 護衞 'bodyguards': the same word with a different Ming gloss. oroγulžu is oro- 'enter' + -γul- + -žu, 'causing to enter'. The sentence continues in the next two units.

words.reading: 阿舌兒中孩-中合撒舌剌 Arγai-Qasar-a

glyphs.s: 阿舌兒中孩-中合撒舌剌

sentences.i: and picked out the brave men for Arqai-Qasar,
sentences.n: Arγai-Qasar-a has the dative -a (Ming 行, 'to'). I read 'for Arqai-Qasar', so the braves are chosen for him as in §191, but 'Arqai-Qasar picked the braves' is the other reading. baγatud is the plural of baγatur 'brave man'. ilγažu 'picking out' as before.

sentences.t: Qalqa-jin Ornuγ̇u-jin Keltegei-Qada-dāča Naiman irgen dür morilarun

morph.gloss: the Qalqa, a river [河名 的]

words.reading: 客勒帖該-中合荅-荅察 Keltegei-Qada-dāča

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in (the Ming glosses it 'time') [行]

sentences.l: Qalqa's, Ornuγ̇u's, from-Keltegei-Qada, Naiman people-against, when-mounting-horse
sentences.i: and when they rode out from Keltegei-Qada in Ornu'u on the Qalqa river against the Naiman people,
sentences.n: The place chain is as in §191, now with the ablative -dāča (Ming 處, 'from'). Naiman irgen is 'the Naiman people' (Ming 種名 百姓), and dür (Ming 行) here means 'against'. morilarun is mori 'horse' + -la- + -run: 'when mounting', Ming 上馬時. The print leaves the sentence open at the section break: §193 starts again with the date and with morilarun, so I do not complete it.

sentences.t: quiluγana žil žun-u teriġün sara-jin harban žirγoγ̇an üdür
sentences.l: Rat year, summer's first month's ten six day,
sentences.i: In the Year of the Rat, on the sixteenth day of the first month of summer,
sentences.n: quiluγana (Ming 鼠兒, 'rat') names the year. žun-u teriġün sara-jin is 'of summer's first month' (teriġün is 'head, first', Ming 頭; sara is 'moon, month'). harban žirγoγan is 'ten six', that is, sixteen: tens first, then units, which is the opposite of English order.

morph.gloss: to sprinkle, make an offering (inferred from the Ming 'sacrifice') [祭祀了]

sentences.i: having made an offering to the standard in the red light, as they mounted,
sentences.n: hulaγan tergel-e is 'red' + tergel 'light, ray' (Ming 光) + the dative-locative -e: 'in the red light'. I take it to mean sunrise, but the Ming does not say so and that is uncertain. tuγ is the standard (Ming 旄纛). sačuγad (Ming 祭祀了, 'having sacrificed') has a stem sača- 'sprinkle' that I guess from its use. morilarun as in §192: 'when mounting'.

sentences.t: Kelüren öġede Žebe, Qubilai qojar-i alginčilažu jabuγ̇ad

morph.gloss: vanguard (stem inferred from the Ming) [頭做着]

sentences.l: Kelüren against, Žebe, Qubilai two-ACC vanguard-making, having-gone,
sentences.i: going up the Kerülen with Jebe and Qubilai, the two, as vanguard,
sentences.n: Kelüren is a river (Ming 河名); I give it as Kerülen. öġede (Ming 逆着, 'against') I read as 'against the current, upstream', which is uncertain. alginčilažu (Ming 頭做着, 'making head') is alginči 'vanguard' (inferred; not glossed) + -la- + -žu: 'making the vanguard'. qojar-i is 'the two' with the accusative. Žebe and Qubilai are men's names (Ming 人名). jabuγad is 'having gone', the converb in -γad.

words.reading: 撒阿舌里-客額舌里 Saγ̇ari-Keġer-i

sentences.i: When they reached Sa'ari-Keger,
sentences.n: kürüġesü is kür- 'reach' + -ġesü 'if, when' (Ming 到呵, 'on reaching'). The place takes the accusative (Ming 行). Saγari-Keger is a place name (Ming 地名); I do not translate it.

sentences.t: Qaṅγar-Qan-u terġü-de Naiman-u qaraγ̇ul tende ažuγ̇u.

words.reading: 中康中合舌兒-中合訥 Qaṅγar-Qan-u

sentences.l: Qaṅγar-Qan's head-at, Naiman's scout there was.
sentences.i: a Naiman scout was there at the head of Mount Qanghar-Qan.
sentences.n: terġü-de is terġü 'head, front' (Ming 頭行) + -de 'at': 'at the head of Qaṅγar-Qan', which the Ming calls a mountain (山名). It is not the word teriġün of the date, though the Ming glosses both as 頭. qaraγul is 'scout, watchman' (Ming 哨望的). ažuγu is a- 'be' + -žuγu, a past of reported fact (Ming 有來, 'there was').

sentences.i: He and our scouts chased one another,
sentences.n: qaraγul-a has the dative -a, here 'with' (Ming 行). hüldeldüžü is hülde- 'chase' (Ming 逐) + -ldü- (each other) + -žü: 'chasing each other'. The subject is not stated; I take it as the Naiman scout and ours. This reading is uncertain.

sentences.t: bidan-u qaraγ̇ul-ača nigen šiṅγula mori maγ̇uqan emeġeltü-ji
sentences.l: Our scouts-from one white horse poor saddled-having-ACC
sentences.i: and from our scouts one poor white horse with a saddle
sentences.n: -ača is the ablative 'from' (Ming 行). nigen 'one'; šiṅγula (Ming 白, 'white') is a colour word I cannot check, so 'white' is the Ming's, not mine; mori 'horse'. maγuqan is maγu 'bad' (Ming 歹) with the diminutive -qan: 'poor'. emeġeltü-ji is emeġel 'saddle' (Ming 鞍子) + -tü 'having' + the accusative -ji. The accusative is odd on the object of a passive verb (next unit, Ming 被), which the Ming copies.

sentences.i: was taken by the Naiman scouts.
sentences.n: abtažuγui is ab- 'take' + -ta- (passive) + -žuγui, a past of reported fact: 'was taken' (Ming 被要了有). The agent, qaraγul-a, is in the dative, 'by' (Ming 行).

sentences.t: Naiman-u qaraγ̇ul tere morin abču ügüleldürün:
sentences.l: Naiman's scouts that horse taking, speaking-together when:
sentences.i: The Naiman scouts took that horse and said to one another:
sentences.n: ügüleldürün is ügüle- 'speak' + -ldü- (together) + -rün 'when' (Ming 共說); the colon opens the speech. morin is the form of mori 'horse' used here (Ming 馬). abču is ab- 'take' + the converb -ču.

sentences.i: "The Mongols' geldings are lean," they said together.
sentences.n: Moṅγol-un is the genitive 'of the Mongols'; the Ming writes 達達 (Tatars) for it, a Ming habit that I do not carry into the English. turuγad is turuγ 'lean' (Ming 瘦) with the plural -ad; ažuγu 'were, are' as in unit 40. keġeldüžüġüi is keġe- 'say' + -ldü- + -žüġüi (past of reported fact): 'they said together'. The mark after ažuγu closes the speech.

words.reading: 撒阿舌里-客額舌里 Saγ̇ari-Keġer-i

sentences.i: When our own men had reached Sa'ari-Keger and halted there,
sentences.n: Bidan-u-γai is 'our' with a particle -γai that the Ming does not gloss (it gives only 的); I take it as emphatic, 'our own', which is uncertain. The story returns to the Mongols here. kürčü 'reaching' (kür- + -čü); toridčü 'halting' (Ming 止着), the stem torid- being known to me only from the Ming.

sentences.i: and were talking over what to do,
sentences.n: ker is 'how' (Ming 怎); kikün is ki- 'do' with the participle -kün (Ming 做). keġeldüġesü is keġe- 'say' + -ldü- (together) + -ġesü 'if, when': 'when talking it over'.

morph.gloss: a man's name [人名 官名]

words.reading: 成吉思-中合中罕-納 Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the ruler's name [太祖︀ 皇帝 行]

words.reading: 都︀舌剌惕中合舌侖 duradγarun

morph.gloss: to remind, bring up (stem uncertain) [提說]

sentences.i: Dodai-Cherbi spoke up to Chinggis Qahan:
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a is one word in the print, with the dative -(n)a (Ming 行, 'to'). duradγarun (Ming 提說, 'bringing up, mentioning'): the stem I do not know, it looks like durad-, and -run is 'when'. The colon opens the speech; the print puts no opening mark here, and the closing mark is in unit 59. I supply the opening mark in the English, before 'We are few'.

morph.gloss: the pronoun's linking n plus -lu, 'only, just' (uncertain)

sentences.i: "We are few.
sentences.n: bidan-lu is bida 'we' (inclusive) with a linking n and -lu, to which the Ming adds 但 'only': I read it as 'we alone' (uncertain). čüġen 'few, little' (Ming 少). bi (Han 備; the Ming gloss is 有) is 'is, are', not the pronoun 'I'; it has this sense wherever it ends a clause in this part.

sentences.i: Besides being few, we have come weary.
sentences.n: deġere is 'on, above, in addition' (Ming 上); čiležü is 'being weary' (Ming 困乏着), the stem čile- being inferred; irebe is ire- 'come' + -be.

sentences.i: Let us halt here like this until our geldings have eaten their fill,
sentences.n: ein is 'thus' (Ming 這般) and kü 'also'. aγtas(i)-jan is aγta + the plural -s + Shiratori's (i) and -jan 'our own'. čadtala is čad- 'be sated' (Ming 喫飽) + -tala 'until'. I give the English a 'let us' because the finite verb is the hortative oγžadγaja in unit 54: all the converbs up to there are steps of one proposal.

words.reading: 撒阿舌里-客額舌里 Saγ̇ari-Keġer-i

sentences.i: spread out over this Sa'ari-Keger and camp,
sentences.n: delgen is 'spread out, wide' (Ming 展開), used as an adverb; baγužu is baγu- 'camp' + -žu. The accusative of the place is the Ming's 行.

sentences.t: amitu ele küġün tutum ere-jin tabun aṅgida γal-nuγ̇ud tüležü
sentences.l: Living every person each, man's five places-at fires burning,
sentences.i: and let every living man light fires in five places,
sentences.n: amitu is ami 'life' + -tu 'having' (Ming 性命有的): 'living'. ele küġün tutum is 'every single man' (ele, Ming 但; tutum, Ming 每 'each'). ere-jin tabun aṅgida: ere 'man' (Ming 男子) with the genitive -jin, 'five places', so 'five places for each man'. aṅgida is 'at places' (Ming 處); the stem aṅgi is a guess. γal-nuγud is 'fires' with a plural in -nuγud (Ming 火每). tüležü is tüle- 'burn' (Ming 燒着) + -žü.

morph.gloss: to give a false alarm (stem inferred from the Ming) [虛驚]

sentences.i: and so give them a false alarm with the fires.
sentences.n: γal(i)-jar is γal 'fire' + the instrumental -(i)-jar 'with' (the Ming 敎火 has 敎, 'cause', in it). oγžadγaja is the stem oγžadγa- 'give a false alarm' (Ming 虛驚, 'false fright'; the stem is inferred) + -ja, the hortative 'let us', as taija was in §189. The false alarm is on the Naiman; nothing in the line says whom, I infer it from the plan.

sentences.i: The Naiman people are said to be many;
sentences.n: keġegdemüi is keġe- 'say' + -gde- (passive) + -mü(i) (present): 'it is said' (Ming 被說有). Who says it is open.

sentences.t: Qān an-u ger-tēče ese γaruγsan taṅgi keġegdemüi.

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
not (negative of a past verb) [不曾]

sentences.l: Qān his tent-from not gone-out weak is-said.
sentences.i: and their Qan, who has never gone out from his tent, is said to be weak.
sentences.n: an-u is 'his' (Ming 他的), the back-vowel partner of in-ü. ger-tēče is ger 'tent' with the ablative, the long ē as printed (Ming 家處). ese γaruγsan: ese 'not' (Ming 不曾) + γaruγsan, the past participle, 'one who has not gone out'. taṅgi is 'weak, feeble' (Ming 弱). This is hearsay (keġegdemüi) about the Naiman Qan, who is named Tayang at the end of the part.

sentences.t: γal(i)-jar hülürigeġültele bidan-u aγtas ber čadumu-že.

words.reading: 忽魯舌里格兀勒帖列 hülürigeġültele

morph.gloss: to be dazed (stem inferred from the Ming) [幌惚間]
to be full, sated [飽有 也者︀]

sentences.l: Fire-with while-dazing, our geldings also full-indeed.
sentences.i: While the fire has them dazed, our geldings too will be full.
sentences.n: hülürigeġültele (Ming 幌惚間, 'in a daze') I take as hülürige- 'be dazed' with the causative -ġül- and -tele 'while': 'while [the fire] dazes [them]'. The stem is inferred and the reading uncertain. ber is 'also' (Ming 也). čadumu-že is čad- 'be full' + a present ending + -že (Ming 也者, 'indeed'); the ending and the particle are taken from the Ming and are uncertain.

sentences.t: aγtas(i)-jan čadγan Naiman-u qaraγ̇ul-i hüldeġed daručažu

morph.gloss: the Naiman, a people [種名 的]
to press hard (stem inferred from the Ming) [緊逐着]

sentences.l: Our-geldings fed-full, Naiman scouts-ACC driving, pressing-hard,
sentences.i: Once our geldings are fed, we drive off the Naiman scouts and press them hard,
sentences.n: čadγan is čad- + -γa- (causative, 'to feed full', Ming 敎飽了) + -n; hüldeġed is hülde- 'chase, drive off' (Ming 趕了) with the converb -ġed; daručažu is 'pressing hard' (Ming 緊逐着), the stem inferred. The whole chain hangs on the question in the next unit.

sentences.t: γol-dur an-u neileġülün tere samaγ̇ui-dur qadqulduγ̇asu bolqu-ju"

morph.gloss: their, his (third-person genitive, back-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀阿速 qadqulduγ̇asu

sentences.l: Centre-in his causing-to-join, that confusion-in if-fight, will-it-do?"
sentences.i: and, joining with his main body in the middle, if we fight in that confusion, will it serve?"
sentences.n: Uncertain. γol-dur is γol 'centre' (Ming 中軍, 'the army's centre') + -dur 'in'. neileġülün is neile- 'join, meet' (Ming 相合) + -ġül- + -n: 'making join'; an-u 'his' (Ming 他的) is the enemy's or ours, I do not know which. samaγui is 'confusion' (Ming 亂). qadqulduγasu is 'if we fight' (Ming 厮殺呵). bolqu-ju is bol- 'be' + -qu + -ju, which I take as a question (Ming 中 麽有, 'will it do?'). The mark after bolqu-ju closes Dodai's speech.

words.reading: 都︀舌剌惕中合阿速 duradγaγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to remind, bring up (stem uncertain) [提說呵]

sentences.i: When he had spoken so,
sentences.n: keġen duradγaγasu is 'saying, when he put it' (Ming 提說呵). -γasu is the conditional on a verb in -γa- (the stem duradγa-, as in unit 48).

sentences.t: ene üge-ji žöbšiježü Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: to approve, say 'right' (stem read from the Ming) [道是着]

sentences.l: This word-ACC approving, Čiṅgis Qaγan decree when-making:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan approved the word and issued a decree:
sentences.n: ene üge-ji žöbšiježü is the same clause as the first line of §191; here the word approved is Dodai's. žarliγ bolurun as in unit 19: 'issued a decree:', the colon opening the speech.

morph.gloss: imperative, second person plural (front-vowel form of -qun)

sentences.i: "Then so be it: light the fires," he said,
sentences.n: tein is 'thus, in that way' (Ming 那般); böġed (Ming 便) is a particle I read as 'then', which is uncertain. tüleġülüdkün is tüle- 'burn' + -ġül- (causative) + -d- (plural subject, uncertain) + -kün, the front-vowel form of the imperative -qun for several persons: 'you all make burn' (Ming 敎燒您). The mark after tüleġülüdkün closes the speech; the speaker is Chinggis.

morph.gloss: to hand on, proclaim (stem uncertain) [傳了]

sentences.i: He gave the order to the troops.
sentences.n: čeriġüd-te is čeri 'army, soldier' + -ġüd (plural) + -te 'to' (Ming 行). žasaγ is 'rule, order' (Ming 軍法, 'military law'); tuṅγaba (Ming 傳了, 'passed on, proclaimed') has a stem tuṅγa- that I do not know.

morph.gloss: so much, that much; thereupon [卽便]

words.reading: 撒阿舌里-客額舌里 Saγ̇ari-Keġer-i

sentences.i: At once, spread out over Sa'ari-Keger and encamped,
sentences.n: tedüi is glossed 卽便 here, 'at once, thereupon' (Ming 那些 'that much' in §192), so I give it as 'thereupon, at once'. The words repeat the proposal in units 52 and following: the order is carried out as spoken.

sentences.t: amitu ele küġün tabun aṅgida γal-nuγ̇ud tüleġülbe.
sentences.l: Living every person five places-at fires burn-caused.
sentences.i: every living man had fires burned in five places.
sentences.n: tüleġülbe is tüle- 'burn' + -ġül- + the past -be, 'had them burned'; the same stem as tüleġülüdkün. The earlier plan said 'each man, five places' (tutum, ere-jin); this line omits those two words, in the Ming too. The point is that the order was carried out, and the fires counted by the man.

sentences.t: Süni Naiman-u qaraγ̇ul Qaṅγar-Qan-u teriġün-eče süni olon γal üžežü"

words.reading: 中康中合舌兒-中合訥 Qaṅγar-Qan-u

sentences.l: Night Naiman's scout Qaṅγar-Qan's head-from night many fire seeing"
sentences.i: That night the Naiman scout, from the top of Qanghar-Qan, saw many fires in the night
sentences.n: teriġün-eče is the ablative of teriġün 'head, top' (Ming 頭處, 'from the head'). üžežü is üže- 'see' (Ming 見着) + -žü. A mark closes after üžežü with none open; the Ming does not help. I treat it as stray and give no quotation here, but it may signal that the scouts' report begins at Süni. The line is uncertain on that.

sentences.i: and said, "The Mongols are not few."
sentences.n: čüġeken is 'a little' (čüġen 'few' with a diminutive -ken; Ming 少); ese-kü 'not' (ese, Ming 不曾, with kü, 也): 'not a little'. Moṅγol-i has the accusative where English wants a subject (Ming 行). keġen büleġe is 'saying, was': 'was saying, said' (bü- 'be' + the past -leġe, Ming 有來). I added the quotation marks myself.

sentences.i: "They have more fires than there are stars," they said,
sentences.n: hodun-(n)ača is hodun 'star' (Ming 星) with the ablative -(n)ača, here 'than'. olon γaltan is 'many fire-having ones' (γaltan: γal 'fire' + -tan, plural 'having'; Ming 火(有的)每). bi (Han 備; the Ming gloss is 有) 'is, are'. The mark after bi closes a speech. keġen 'saying' ends it. The print closes a speech after bi but opens none; I supply the opening mark at Hodun-(n)ača.

sentences.t: Tajaṅ Qān-dur maγ̇utu emeġeltü šiṅγulaqan morin ögčü: ileġed
sentences.l: Tajaṅ Qān-to poor saddled whitish horse giving: having-gone,
sentences.i: and gave a poor, saddled, whitish horse to Tayang Qan, and, going to him, said:
sentences.n: The colon after ögčü (Ming 與着, 'giving') leads into the speech. Qān-dur has the dative -dur (Ming 行, 'to'). maγutu (Ming 歹(有的), 'bad'), emeġeltü 'saddled' and šiṅγulaqan (Ming 白小, with the diminutive) all qualify morin; the horse is the one taken from our scouts in units 42-43. ileġed (Ming 去了, 'gone') is ile- with the converb -ġed; ile- can mean 'go' or 'send', and I do not know which is meant here. Uncertain. The glossary reads ile- as 'to send' (an earlier Ming 敎去了, 'caused to go'), so 'having sent' is also possible here.

words.reading: 撒阿舌里-客額舌里 Saγ̇ari-Keġer-i

morph.gloss: to be complete, fill up [塞滿]

sentences.i: "The Mongol armies have come down, filling Sa'ari-Keger.
sentences.n: bütetele is büte- 'be complete, fill' (Ming 塞滿, 'stuffed full') + -tele 'until, so that': 'so as to fill'. baγuluγa is baγu- 'camp, come down' (Ming 下了來) + a past of reported fact. Moṅγol-un čeriġüd is 'the Mongols' armies' (Ming 達達的軍每). The quote marks here are mine; the print opens none in this stretch.

sentences.t: Üdür-tür ündürün aqun-u Hodun-(n)ača olon γaltan bi"

morph.gloss: 'are there?' (analysis uncertain; probably from a-, to be) [有的麽]

sentences.l: Day-in increasing are-they? Stars-than many fire-having are"
sentences.i: By day they keep on increasing. They have more fires than there are stars."
sentences.n: Üdür-tür is 'in the day' (Ming 日裏). ündürün is 'increasing' (Ming 增添) with a stem ündür- that I do not know. aqun-u (Ming 有的麽, 'are there?') I do not analyse; the Ming's 麽 could be a question, 'are they increasing by day?', or I may have got the force wrong. The mark after bi closes the speech.

sentences.i: So saying, they went.
sentences.n: keġežü iležüġüi is 'saying … went' (ile- 'go', Ming 去了; the past -žüġüi). Whether the scouts went to Tayang with the report or sent word depends on how ileġed is read in unit 69, and I cannot settle it. The part ends with the Mongols camped and burning fires and the Naiman scouts bringing the report. The glossary reads ile- as 'to send', so 'they sent' is also possible.
